[OPINION][PHP] What is your opinion about PHP in today's programming?
It means PHP sucks, is held in extremely low regard, and you should avoid it.
As a dev, I prefer the opposite. You must learn it in order to know what it means to be a good language and bad (insufficient) one.

Here's a great post on exactly why php sucks. It's a few years old, but languages don't change that fast. It's still entirely relevant.

On the other hand, there must be a reason so much of the web runs on php. Maybe it's just because pretty much everyone has some experience with it, so it's always the one thing everyone is willing to work with? I'm not sure. Regardless, if you want a programming job, php is a good language to get used to, just because so many things use it.

I just won't use it for my own projects.

The reason of much of the web runs on php must be because it's free. Many people used it (the community is big and resources are much). Many shared hosting running PHP, maybe because the setup is easy and the interface (cpanel) is fulfilling the needs.

IMO, the language is easy to learn at entry level, making it suitable language for beginners.

And whoa, that article sure is long. Looks like the author's dislike for PHP is great.

Being free is not the main reason many people used it. Many languages are free to use. It was free, simple, and solved the problem of dynamic web pages.

Now javascript and browser features have developed allowing for single page apps and other powerful dynamic content, PHP is not needed to solve that problem. It is still a usable langauge and several old and mature products such as wordpress and mediawiki need it. It is not going away quickly because of this. However I can not imagine a new project that you benefit using it for.

I would say that PHP is an attractive trap for the unwary. PHP is extremely good at one thing: getting a webpage with some server side processing up and running in the shortest time possible. It's very easy to get started with since it doesn't force you to consider for example the types of your variables, it just tries to do the right thing.

Here's the thing though: quick doesn't mean extensible or good. You can build a house from wood but good luck trying to turn it into a skyscraper. In PHP you typically get started by writing a file which you can then execute by visiting it in your webbrowser. This is nice and quick. But then you want to have nice URL's (e.g. /v/askdev/new) and then you either funnel everything to a single .php file (which loses the benefit of .php files being easy to execute) or have a whole bunch of rules in your webserver configuration which send visitors to URLs like this to this .php file and visitors to URLs like that to that .php file.

Modern PHP seems to use web frameworks which handle all the routing and trivial stuff for you. However every language under the sun seems to have such web frameworks so you lose the benefits of PHP compared to other languages. You do however keep the downsides.

And there are plenty of downsides. PHP has a "lets try to keep it running" attitude that many times leads to it silently doing something different than you intended. Where decent programming languages have an attitude of "fail quickly, fail loudly" (so that you can catch bugs early in development) PHP usually tries to sweep errors under the carpet or report them in such a way that it's hard to know if something is an error. For example json_decode("true") returns true (PHP boolean value), json_decode("null") returns NULL (PHP null value) and json_decode("totally@invalid_json!") returns NULL, so NULL is both used as a valid return value and as the indication of an error. Compare this to Python where json.loads("null") returns None (Python null value) and json_decode("invalid") throws an exception or Go where you get a second return value indicating the error.

For new programmers PHP is a really bad starting language since it teaches sloppy programming. Use a string as an integer, sure, what could go wrong (quick: what's "a"+1)?

Since most good programmers avoid PHP a lot of answers to PHP questions you find on the internet (or in the comments in the manual, or in the main text of the manual) are wrong. I just searched for how to include parameters in an SQL query and sure enough three of seven answers (newest from March this year (!)) that says use string interpolation (i.e. `"INSERT INTO mytable VALUES ($foo, $bar)") or equivalent. Sure, four of seven answers (including the top and accepted one with 30 votes) did warn about SQL injection but if people seriously suggest using a method that's very famous for causing security woes in 2015 how do you know that for a less obvious question the information is correct? Note that in other languages like Python this whole issue never pops up since it's easier to correctly invoke the SQL interface than incorrectly.

In summary, to answer the question succinctly: my opinion is that PHP is the worst programming language in common use.
